stimulus.text:
“His Britannic Majesty acknowledges the said United States, viz., New Hampshire, Massachusetts Bay, Rhode Island and Providence Plantations, Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Delaware, Maryland, Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina and Georgia, to be free sovereign and independent states, that he treats with them as such, and for himself, his heirs, and successors, relinquishes all claims to the government, propriety, and territorial rights of the same and every part thereof.”
—Treaty of Paris, Article 1, September 3, 1783 (abridged)
stimulus.source_note: Treaty of Paris, September 3, 1783. Public domain.

books.section: Topic 3.5 The American Revolution, A. The War for Independence

stem: Which of the following was a provision of the Treaty of Paris of 1783?

options.text: Canada and Quebec were ceded to the United States
options.misconception: Canada stayed British; the treaty drew the boundary along the Great Lakes and left Quebec in British hands.

options.text: The Mississippi became the western boundary of the United States
Britain kept the lands west of the Appalachian Mountains
options.misconception: Britain ceded the trans-Appalachian west to the United States, with the Mississippi as the boundary.

options.text: The United States paid Britain for its independence
options.misconception: The United States paid nothing for independence; Britain recognized it and gave up its claims.

rationales.B: The treaty ceded Britain's lands between the Appalachians and the Mississippi to the United States, making the river the new nation's western edge.
rationales.A: Canada was not ceded; it remained British, and the boundary ran along the Great Lakes.
rationales.C: The west went to the Americans, not to Britain; the treaty moved the boundary to the Mississippi.
rationales.D: No payment bought independence; Britain acknowledged it and relinquished its claims.
rationales.general:
1. Read what Britain gives up. All claims to government and territory over the named states, every part of them.
2. Ask about the map. The treaty also moved the nation's western edge to the Mississippi River.
3. Rule out the rest. Canada stayed British, the west changed hands toward America, and no one paid for independence.
Remember: a peace treaty is a map as well as a sentence — ask what land changed hands. Background: the treaty also gave Americans fishing rights off Newfoundland and promised Loyalists a chance to recover confiscated property.
